title: I don't dislike the Avatar franchise but I'm just not a misanthrope

commenti.body: I hated the first Avatar and it blows my mind that he got away with remaking the same movie with modern technology and calling it a sequel instead of a reboot.  I think that people just know they need to love James Cameron movies because they're going to be super successful and everyone's going to talk about loving them. Somehow those Rose colored glasses have just never come off. I'm a big fan of a lot of his older movies though

It seems like demoralization porn to me, propaganda. I could be mistaken but there seems to be a concerted effort to get young people to hate society and themselves, without really offering a path out of the labyrinth. 

Like "we're greed obsessed" or "humanity is a virus" ideas like that are easy pills to swallow. I don't know I can't really articulate my thoughts right now but it seems like screws are being turned on us, and we've never been more demoralized or self loathing, it doesn't seem organic and it doesn't seem helpful, to me anyway

I can't speak for everyone, but I enjoyed both of these movies.

The plot is not going to blow anyone away, but the world of Avatar is beautiful and unique. Point to me a movie that has a world similar to Avatar and made it look as good. The animals look cool, the Na'vi culture speaks to me, the floating islands in the first movie were fun, exploring the underwater world in the second movie was exciting, and the list goes on.

To me, the plot is just a device that allows us to explore the world. If you watch the movie on a 32" screen, then I understand why you wouldn't enjoy it. But watching it on an IMAX screen, it's mesmerizing. It's easily worth the $20 ticket.

It is not easy to make a film that looks as good as Avatar does, so I appreciate it for what it is: a beautiful, world-building movie with a sub-par plot. It's not perfect, but it's enjoyable, and that's all I can really ask of a film.
The water level sucked but avatar one was a pretty fun action/adventure film. As for your point about not finding a human good guy to root for? Just look at human history there often isn’t.
